headline: On last trading day, Sensex crashed 1,000 points as foreign investors sold en-masse, wiping out ₹9 lakh crore.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: En-masse selling by foreign institutional investors
Global concerns over rate hikes and rising oil prices
Surging US Treasury yields impacting global market sentiment
Benchmark shares recording their longest weekly losing run in 25 years
whatHappening: The Sensex plummeted over 1,000 points in the last session, resulting in a ₹9.5 lakh crore loss in investor wealth
The Nifty 50 index slipped below the 22,300 level during the previous day's heavy sell-off
Government authorities capped sugar stock limits for dealers at 1,000 quintals ahead of the festive season
Indian Bank is considering a waiver of the 0.28% MDR on UPI transactions according to its CEO
summary: The Indian stock market suffered a major crash in its last session, with the Sensex falling 1,000 points amid heavy foreign investor selling. This downturn marked the longest weekly losing streak in 25 years and the worst monthly performance since March. Markets are currently closed for an NSE holiday and will reopen on Monday.
